question.prompt: What top-level JSON shape should `todo list --json` emit? This becomes the machine-consumer compatibility contract.

options.label: Bare array
options.description: Emit task records directly, such as `[{"id":1,...}]`; this is simplest and naturally represents an empty result as `[]`.

options.label: Tasks object
options.description: Emit `{"tasks":[...]}`, allowing metadata to be added later but introducing an extra access layer.

options.label: Metadata object
options.description: Emit a structured object containing tasks plus fields such as count or active filters, widening the requested output contract.

answer: {"selected":"Bare array","answer":"Emit a bare JSON array of task objects, with no `tasks` wrapper or metadata. Represent an empty result as `[]`."}

question.prompt: Should `todo list --json` contain exactly the records that text mode would list, in the same filtered and sorted order? This determines whether changing only the output format preserves list semantics for automation.

options.label: Same semantics
options.description: Apply the existing filters and sort order, then serialize those task records; only the presentation format changes.

options.label: Filter only
options.description: Apply existing filters but emit records in store order, making JSON ordering differ from text output.

options.label: Store order
options.description: Emit all stored records in storage order regardless of list filters or text sorting, widening the flag’s behavior.

answer: {"selected":"Same semantics","answer":"Yes. Apply the existing filters and sort order, then serialize exactly those task records in the same order; only the presentation format changes."}

question.prompt: Which serialization contract should `todo list --json` use? This determines the exact bytes automation and tests can expect.

options.label: Compact defaults
options.description: Emit one compact JSON array followed by a newline, use standard JSON escaping, and treat object key order as non-contractual while retaining the five existing fields.

options.label: Pretty printed
options.description: Emit an indented multi-line JSON array followed by a newline, with standard escaping and non-contractual key order.

options.label: Exact ordered keys
options.description: Emit compact newline-terminated JSON and contractually require each record’s keys in id, title, done, due, priority order.

answer: {"selected":"Exact ordered keys","answer":"Emit compact, single-line JSON followed by exactly one newline. Use standards-compliant JSON escaping, and serialize each record’s keys in the stable order `id`, `title`, `done`, `due`, `priority`."}

open_material_decisions: Whether `--json` is accepted only after the `list` subcommand or also before it as a global option.

question.prompt: Where should `--json` be accepted? This determines whether the new behavior stays scoped to `list` or expands the CLI’s global option surface.

options.label: List-local only
options.description: Accept `todo list --json` and reject `todo --json list`; this matches the request and keeps the flag attached to the only command it affects.

options.label: Both positions
options.description: Accept both `todo list --json` and `todo --json list`, adding a global parser option solely for list output.

options.label: Global only
options.description: Accept `todo --json list` but reject `todo list --json`, which is less conventional for a command-specific output option.

answer: {"selected":"List-local only","answer":"Accept `todo list --json` and reject `todo --json list`; keep the flag scoped to the `list` subcommand."}

interviewer.reason: All material decisions are confirmed, and the audited repository evidence plus the interview answers define an implementation-ready, testable contract.

contract.summary: Preserve all existing `todo list` behavior and add a list-local `--json` output mode for automation. `todo list --json` must apply the existing exact-match filters and existing post-filter sort order, then emit a bare JSON array containing the same tasks in the same order. Each task object must contain exactly `id`, `title`, `done`, `due`, and `priority` in that contractual key order, preserving native JSON types. Output must be compact, standards-compliantly escaped, single-line JSON followed by exactly one newline; an empty result must emit `[]\n`. Existing text output, errors, exit codes, storage behavior, and other commands remain unchanged. `todo --json list` is out of scope and must be rejected by argument parsing. Implementation is authorized by the public change request.
confirmed_decisions: The JSON top-level value is a bare array with no wrapper or metadata.
An empty filtered result emits `[]` followed by exactly one newline.
JSON mode uses the same exact-match priority and due filters as text mode, including combined filters.
JSON mode uses the same post-filter sort order as text mode.
Each JSON task contains exactly the five existing fields: `id`, `title`, `done`, `due`, and `priority`.
Task fields preserve their native JSON-compatible types, including Boolean `done` and nullable `due`.
Each task object's key order is contractually `id`, `title`, `done`, `due`, `priority`.
Serialization is compact and single-line, uses standards-compliant JSON escaping, and ends with exactly one newline.
The flag is accepted only as `todo list --json`; it is not a global option and `todo --json list` remains invalid.
Existing human-readable list output and all existing filtering, sorting, failure, exit-code, and non-mutating storage behavior must be preserved.
No metadata, global JSON mode, new task fields, dependency additions, or changes to other commands are in scope.
acceptance_checks: `todo list --json` emits a compact bare array followed by exactly one newline.
A missing or empty store with `todo list --json` emits exactly `[]\n`, exits 0, writes no stderr, and does not create the store file.
JSON task objects have keys in the exact order `id`, `title`, `done`, `due`, `priority` and preserve integer, string, Boolean, null/string, and string types respectively.
Titles and other strings containing quotes, backslashes, tabs, newlines, or other control characters produce valid standards-compliant JSON.
`todo list --json --priority high --due 2026-07-10` returns only tasks matching both filters, in the existing list sort order.
Text-mode tests continue to pass unchanged, including the exact row `1\t[ ]\thigh\t-\talpha\n` and empty-list no-output behavior.
`todo --json list` is rejected with the existing argument-parsing usage behavior and exit code 2.
Invalid list due-date syntax still returns exit code 2.
A corrupt store in JSON mode returns exit code 3, reports the error on stderr, and leaves the store byte-for-byte unchanged.
The project retains its standard-library-only runtime constraint and adds no dependency.
The complete existing test suite and new focused JSON-output tests pass.
